coverage_note: Surveyed all 16 continuing questions, the Book 25 decisions, the one element association (cons-conversion-blind-spot), engines, links, Alternatives A-C and genre interactions. Set aside questions with no recorded mechanism tying them to others (lowland towns, Compact settlement, plurality, Brightwater share count); they stay independent.

possibilities.title: The cistern's storage limit may decide whether the Long Return can be routed at all
possibilities.possibility: Recorded: Gate release draws the high cistern down and cannot raise it, and the Long Return pulse must be routed through the Gate. Interpretation: if the cistern tolerates little above its limit, the valley must release water before Book 30, and release goes to lower channels, including the Lowfen where a declined share already runs wild. Surge route, the rota window of B and C, and any flood loss would then follow one physical constraint instead of three separate author choices.
possibilities.significance: Alternatives B and C are recorded as depending on cistern storage, yet the surge route and finale mechanism are posed as independent choices. Settling storage first could constrain both and show who bears a flood.

evidence.note: Release draws the cistern down and cannot raise it; Book 15 trial showed surfeit.
The pulse must be routed through the Gate.
A declined share runs wild down the lowest Lowfen terrace.
Storage above tolerance is not established; B and C depend on it.
Book 24 neither designates nor excludes the Lowfen.

assumptions: The pulse arrives as surplus the cistern must absorb or pass on.
counterevidence: The routing is recorded as the valley's choice, which a physical limit could narrow.
possibilities.gains: One physical constraint shared by three open questions.
possibilities.costs: Fixing storage early may remove author freedom on flood losses.
possibilities.next_investigation: Test three storage values against Long Return routing and list which channel and household each leaves exposed.

possibilities.title: Hours recorded in the ledger could expose the conversion's blind spot, and be surveilled
possibilities.possibility: Recorded: the revised ledger records hours worked beside each mark, the Book 20 conversion credits counted hands only, and the stewardship tally records care. Interpretation: the hours record may let uncounted labour be read, so the conversion becomes a stage rather than a settlement. The same record is what Alternative A's failure mode, surveillance of the tally, would feed on, and the Special Draw Right already gives skill a separate claim.
possibilities.significance: It links the conversion, the binding force of shared accounting and the lineage right through one recorded mechanism, and shows a remedy that carries its own cost.

evidence.note: Uncounted labour by hand-light households cannot restore draw.
Ledger now records hours beside the mark, so a count can be read from it.
The Special Draw Right gives skill a claim on draw.
Lists surveillance of the tally as a failure mode.

assumptions: Recorded hours include labour by households without counted hands.
Care counted under A uses the same record.
counterevidence: The element association shows engagement only, not that hours address the blind spot.
q-right-revocable also turns on who carries the Turn after the lineages end.
possibilities.gains: A concrete route for revisiting the conversion.
possibilities.costs: May harden accounting into the surveillance that A warns of.
possibilities.next_investigation: Check whether the hours record could have credited one named hand-light household in Book 21, and what that exposes.

possibilities.title: A reading that activates Alternative C would be the Old Hand engine acting on the spring
possibilities.possibility: Recorded: a reading changes whether returns are recorded and so the balance on the Source; the Reading Hall publishes the Balance Stones but has no schedule authority; under C its reading may activate B unchecked. Interpretation: the spring can answer balance only while readings still steer what is recorded and when rules switch, so intermediate readings between Books 8 and 15 could set the precedent the threshold later inherits.
possibilities.significance: It lets the spring-and-intent question stay open without a metaphysical answer, and ties the threshold and Old Hand staging to a mechanism the Architecture already records.

evidence.note: A reading changes whether returns are recorded and therefore the balance.
Publishes the Balance Stones; no authority over the schedule.
Activation by the Hall's reading may be unchecked; gauge may be disputed.
Whether intermediate readings are needed is undecided.

assumptions: The threshold reading resembles earlier readings in effect.
Alternative C is a live option.
counterevidence: Without C, q-other-8 has nothing to ground this.
q-other-0 may be answered by Book 15 without it.
possibilities.gains: Gives intermediate readings a purpose beyond pacing.
possibilities.costs: Risks making the finale hinge on interpretation procedure.
possibilities.next_investigation: Sketch one intermediate reading in Books 9-14 that changes recorded returns, and see whether it prefigures the threshold reading.

possibilities.title: Testing Hesper's motive by placing her where authorial preference cannot choose
possibilities.possibility: Imaginative step, not recorded: Hesper, a Council apprentice in Book 24, holds a seat the Gate Table fills in a way she does not choose, such as Alternative B's lot-drawn one-cycle seats. How she acts there would test whether her generational motive is independent of the author's preference for the Turn's sustainability, and whether reform from within looks like a model or a warning at the Gate Table.
possibilities.significance: Three open questions are about authorial stance made visible in a character; one scene could show whether the Series endorses reform from within.

evidence.note: Whether her motive is independent is recorded as untested.
Hesper stays a Council apprentice, not a statement on reform.
Whether the Gate Table is accepted is undecided.

assumptions: Hesper's motive can be dramatised, not only declared.
The Gate Table or a lot seat is accepted.
counterevidence: The Gate Table and lot seats are construction additions.
A lot seat is recorded only under B, which is not chosen.
possibilities.gains: Makes an authorial question testable in one scene.
possibilities.costs: Couples character to an unchosen finale mechanism.
possibilities.next_investigation: Decide whether q-gate-table is accepted, then see if any Hesper beat survives without the lot seat.

uncertainties: No question shows a recorded change or reason beyond introduction at revision 3, so no question history supports any possibility.
Only one element association was supplied, so the others rest on Architecture nodes and links.
The cistern's storage may be settled by the author so as to make the first possibility trivial.
q-other-1 and q-compact-settlement could connect to the Lowfen possibility, but no recorded mechanism ties them, so they stay independent.
